# Proof kits

Proof-driven development: write the proof before the feature. A proof kit
holds everything one PR's proof needs, written out ahead:

- what must be running (the proof database, the embeddings stub, the PR's build),
- the data to prepare, each piece with a check so prepared data is skipped,
- the cases and what counts as working, including cases Claude proposed from
  the PR's diff for the areas next to the change, each approved or rejected
  with the reason kept,
- the captions for the video.

`prove.ts` runs a kit. It checks the needs, prepares only what's missing,
then records the narrated video (the default) or rehearses it live in front
of you. The report and the video are the PR's proof. When the data is
already in place, a run starts in seconds, so a kit is as easy to rerun and
share as a video.

## Run a kit

From `discourse-graph/apps/roam` (for its tsx and playwright):

```bash
PROVE="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/prove.ts"
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --coverage   # the kit against its Done When; opens nothing
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --check   # what's missing, changes nothing
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json           # record the video
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --live    # rehearse it with you
```

- `--coverage` validates the kit and prints its cases by decision and its
  Done When coverage, without a browser, a build or the database, so a
  session writing code can check a kit it just wrote. `--check` opens a
  Roam session to look at the before-load data.
- `/proof-kit <ticket> [stage] [flags]` (the `proof-kit` Claude skill) walks
  a ticket through these commands; its stages and flags are in
  `~/.claude-company/skills/proof-kit/stages.json`, which the
  `proof-kit-band` mod shows above the prompt while you type the command.
- `--kits a.json,b.json` runs several kits one after another with the same
  flags and prints where each report and video landed. A failed kit doesn't
  stop the rest.
- Kits run on slot 3 (test-3-graph). discourse-dev-graph is refused unless
  you pass `--allow-dev-graph`.
- A kit that touches a database needs the proof database up (see below):
  `npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db.ts up`. Runs read its
  keys from `proof/db/.env`; `SUPABASE_*` exported in your shell are ignored.
- Every run writes `output/proof/<kit>-<timestamp>/`: `journal.jsonl` (every
  event), `report.md` (ready to post as a PR comment), plus the video, or the
  proposed kit and the footage for a rehearsal.
- Other flags (`--dist`, `--slot`, `--url`, `--allow-login`,
  `--allow-stale-build`, `--no-narrate`, `--mode`, `--speed`, `--dwell`) are
  listed at the top of `prove.ts`.

What a run does, in order:

1. **Needs.** Each need is checked, and a failure prints the command that
   fixes it. The dist must have the right env baked in, and when the kit names
   a PR, the dist's `buildCommit` must be the PR's head.
2. **Outside fixtures.** Database rows and anything else done from the shell:
   check, apply only if missing, check again.
3. **Before-load fixtures.** Flags and node types, which the extension reads
   once at load. They run in a session without the extension, Roam gets time
   to sync the writes, and a fresh session confirms them.
4. **The session.** In-session fixtures (pages, settings Roam resets on every
   load) and the baseline's smoke checks run first. In a take they're trimmed
   off the video. Then the cases run.
5. **The report.**

## The proof database

Kits never touch the hosted (production) database, and no longer share the
stack you develop against either. They get their own local Supabase:

- **Native, no Docker.** It runs on the Supabase CLI's experimental stack
  (`[experimental] stack = true`), pinned to 2.119.0 in `proof/db/package.json`
  and installed there on first use. Its data lives in `~/.supabase/stacks/`.
- **Its own ports.** The API is `127.0.0.1:55321`, Postgres `55322` (the
  checkout's 543xx moved to 553xx), so it runs beside main's Docker stack on
  54321 and any worktree's. Analytics, mail and edge functions stay off.
  `core/database.ts` holds the address; every path in proof uses it.
- **A checkout's schema.** `db.ts up` writes `proof/db/supabase/` from
  `discourse-graph/packages/database/supabase` (config, migrations, schemas)
  and brings the database to those migrations: new ones apply in place, and
  when one it applied changed or is gone (switching from a PR's worktree back
  to main) it resets. `--from <worktree>` tests a PR's own migrations.
- **Seeded with what kits name.** The dev graph (space 66566) and the
  Obsidian test vault (106039) as publish sources, test-3-graph (120237), each
  with its anonymous account, the authors 3 and 106041, and the
  `eng-2329-demo` group all three are in. Generated ids start at 200000.

```bash
DB="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db.ts"
$DB up [--from <checkout>]   # start, migrate, seed, write proof/db/.env
$DB status                   # answering? which checkout's schema?
$DB reset                    # back to the migrations, seeded again
$DB sql "select id, url from \"Space\""
$DB stop                     # data stays for the next up
```

Builds for kits (`prove.ts --build`) bake in the proof database and the
embeddings stub, or no database at all when it isn't set up and the kit
doesn't need one. They never inherit a dev stack's env or fall back to
discoursegraphs.com's API.

### cases

- `steps`: recordDemo actions, each with a one-line `why`. `source` says who
  wrote a step: `kit`, `model` or `you`. js from `model` or `you` runs only
  after you allow it on the HUD, which sets `approved: true`.
- `intent`: plain language. A case with only an intent needs a live rehearsal,
  where the brain works out its steps.
- `expect.js` runs in the page; throwing fails the case. `expect.text` needs
  your eyes: you give the verdict live, and in a take the video is the
  evidence. A case can be only an `expect.js` check.
- `proves` names the Done When bullet the case covers (see "Done When"
  above); `checks` says in plain words what its `expect.js` checks.
- `decision` is `{ status: proposed | approved | rejected, by, at, reason }`.
  A case without one was written by hand and counts as approved; only
  approved cases run, and a rejected case needs its `reason`. `surface` names
  the area (from the kit's `surface` list) a case checks. `qa.ts` writes both.
- `caption` and `toast` are for the take: the narration line and the
  top-right flash. Write captions the way the pr-video skill says.
- `{ "when": { "js", "do": [actions] } }` runs its actions only when the js
  is truthy, so a toggle (the Discourse context overlay, say) can be turned
  on without turning it off on the next run. Its js counts as js for the
  Allow rule.

### templates

Any string can use `{{env.NAME}}`, `{{kit}}`, `{{run}}` and `{{ns}}`. They're
filled only when the string runs, so keys never land in a kit, a proposed
kit or a generated storyboard on disk.

## Obsidian kits

A kit with `target.app: "obsidian"` (plus `vault`, `cdp`, `pr` and `dist`)
attaches over CDP to an Obsidian you started on the test vault with
`--remote-debugging-port=9223`, and records through `recordObsidian.ts`.
Takes and `--check` only; live rehearsals drive Roam. No baseline and no
before-load fixtures, since the app is already running. `--build` builds
apps/obsidian in the PR's worktree with the local database and the stub,
stages it in `dist` with `build-commit.txt`, and installs `main.js` and
`styles.css` in the vault, keeping the replaced files as `*.pre-<kit>`. A
take rebuilds and reinstalls when the vault runs another kit's build, and
reloads the plugin before anything else. `proof.obsidian` has the vault
helpers: `nodeType`, `importedFiles`, `removeNodeTypes`, `open`, `write`,
`setTemplates`, `notices`, `closeModals`. The palette action types into
Obsidian's palette.

## Take: the video

The default. It needs nobody at the screen, so it refuses a kit with
intent-only cases, js you haven't allowed, or cases still waiting for a
decision, and says which. It writes a
small storyboard module that builds the storyboard from the kit when
recordDemo loads it, then runs `recorder/recordDemo.ts --narrate --cursor`
unchanged. Fixtures and smoke checks go in the storyboard's `setup`, which
recordDemo runs before scene 1 and trims off the video. The report marks each
case pass, fail, shown (checked by eye, see the video) or not run, with the
time it starts in the video (`video 1:05`), and says when setup or the video
assembly failed instead. The recorder logs each scene's start in the finished
video and embeds them as chapters in the mp4, so a player can jump from case
to case.

## Live: a rehearsal you steer

`--live` runs the kit in front of you on workspace 9. Steps the kit knows
replay through recordDemo's `runAction` with no model involved. A case written
only as an intent, a failed step, or something you ask for in chat goes to the
brain: a Claude Code session, ideally on Haiku, told to read this file. What
works is baked into `kit.proposed.json`. Review it with `diff -u`, and move it
over the kit to keep it. The rehearsal's report gives each case's time in the
session footage (`footage 4:10`), so a by-hand test has its place in the
recording. The session stays open after the last case so you can
add cases, and ends when you press Stop twice on the HUD or the brain sends
`stop`.
